Independent reproduction from the #2168 Step 9c gate (2026-08-18) — same root cause, arrived at
independently, plus a CONTROLLED EXPERIMENT that removes the last inferential step.

This task's evidence is arithmetic inference from junit timings (22.2 min drift -> "marker age 28m",
4 failures in the api-error probe family). #2168 hit the same file at a LONGER drift and the failure set
grew monotonically, which is the prediction this root cause makes:
  #2158: ~22.2 min drift ->  4 failures
  #2168: ~38   min drift -> 12 failures (the 4 above PLUS the human-activity, heartbeat, streak,
         runaway-flag and main-verdict-line cases, whose slack is larger so they need more drift)
Observed ages matched the arithmetic exactly: a 3600 s (60 m) fixture marker reported as "98m" (60+38),
a ~1 m marker as "39m".

CONTROLLED EXPERIMENT (the part inference could not supply). A pytest plugin that ages ONLY
test_tick_triage.NOW at pytest_collection_finish, changing no code and no other state:
    #2168 branch tip,                    drift    0 s -> 127 passed
    #2168 branch tip,                    drift 2280 s ->  12 failed  (exactly the gate's 12, name-for-name)
    origin/main's scripts/tick_triage.py, drift    0 s -> 127 passed
    origin/main's scripts/tick_triage.py, drift 2280 s ->  12 failed  (identical set)
So MAIN'S OWN CODE fails identically under the same elapsed time. Wall-clock is sufficient to produce the
whole failure set, and no branch content is necessary. The swapped file was restored immediately and the
worktree verified clean.

This also confirms this task's "evades the Step 9c compare" analysis from the other direction: #2168's
per-file pristine oracle would likewise have classified these 12 as NEW, because a per-file re-run
executes within minutes of collection and structurally cannot reproduce the drift.

One addition to the fix scope: the repo-wide sweep this task proposes should look for module-level clock
captures generally, not only the literal `^NOW = time.time()` spelling — any module-scope
time.time()/datetime.now() bound at import and later compared against a live clock has the same failure
mode, and the sweep is cheap to widen while the fix is open.

Filed from #2168 as corroboration; NOT a duplicate task, per the (target_file, fingerprint) dedup rule.
